topic: Philosophy of Religion: Religious Experience, Problem of Evil
subject: religious-studies

moments.title: Of Miracles
moments.who: David Hume, Enquiry concerning Human Understanding
moments.body: Section X of the Enquiry (1748) argues that no testimony to a miracle can ever justify belief. The wise calibrate belief to evidence; testimony to violation of laws of nature is always less probable than the testimony's falseness or mistake.
moments.takeaway: Hume's miracles argument has been continuously debated. Modern Bayesian formulations (Earman 'Hume's Abject Failure', 2000) attempt to either rescue or refute it.

moments.title: Dialogues Concerning Natural Religion
moments.body: Hume wrote the Dialogues over decades; they were published posthumously (1779). Three characters — Demea (orthodox), Cleanthes (natural theologian, design argument), Philo (sceptic, often Hume's voice) — debate. The design argument is subjected to its most thorough early criticism.

quote.text: What peculiar privilege has this little agitation of the brain which we call thought, that we must thus make it the model of the whole universe?

moments.takeaway: Hume's design critique anticipates Darwin (who provided the alternative mechanism). The problem of evil also takes its modern form in the Dialogues.

moments.title: Hume's death
moments.who: Adam Smith and the Edinburgh circle
moments.body: August 1776: Hume dies in Edinburgh. Adam Smith's letter to William Strahan describes Hume's death — calm, sceptical, refusing the deathbed conversion expected of unbelievers. The letter caused outrage in religious circles.
moments.takeaway: Hume's serene death was as much a public argument as his books — a model of philosophical equanimity without religious consolation.

now.title: Hume's lasting influence
now.body: Hume is the canonical philosopher of religious scepticism. Modern atheism (Dennett, Dawkins) draws on his arguments; modern theistic responses (Plantinga, Swinburne) engage them. The Dialogues remain on philosophy of religion syllabuses worldwide.
now.open_questions: Was Hume an atheist or a deist? Almost certainly an atheist or close to it. His public caution reflected his time; his private letters and posthumous works clarify his views.

reflection: The Scottish Enlightenment's leading philosopher subjected natural religion to systematic critique. Hume's arguments — about miracles, design, the problem of evil — remain the framework in which modern philosophy of religion operates.
